summary: All three items resolved. (1) The suspended add() was a debugging leftover, not a hold — established from artifacts, then confirmed by the Product Owner before touching it: it exists only in the working tree (HEAD has always had the live call), its message names the wrong entity ('WeddingConfigPublic' inside the admin WeddingConfig service — copy-pasted from the sibling), it uses none of this repo's two documented hold idioms (readOnly() with a task ref, notImplemented()), the API still exposes POST /v1/config to bride/groom, and nothing anywhere calls weddingConfigCollection.add(), so there was no misbehaviour to hold back. Restored in place; the file is now byte-identical to HEAD, so there is nothing to commit for it. (2) release.ts: the 'committed placeholder' the task points at is itself a stale hash (f4ee01c), not the 'dev' placeholder the file's docstring and the generator both claim is committed — restoring literally would have reinstated the same misread-as-released-commit hazard. Committed 'dev' instead, with the PO's approval. (3) Fixed the unused WeddingGuestsService import rather than widening rule 11's clause; CLAUDE.md deliberately untouched. Lint 6 -> 4, exactly the documented modal errors. e2e is NOT green: 9 failures, every one the T389 ds-kit harness timeout, in specs nothing here touches.

deviations.from: Restore src/environments/release.ts to the committed placeholder.
deviations.reason: The committed value is not a placeholder. It is f4ee01c ('docs(tasks): T360 report records its own commit hash'), a stale build stamp that entered history in 535428d — while the file's own docstring and scripts/generate-release.mjs:7-10 both state the committed value is a 'dev' placeholder. Restoring literally would have swapped one commit hash for another and reinstated the exact hazard the task names — a hash in a checked-out tree reads as the released commit — while producing a zero diff and therefore no commit for a bullet that asks for one. 'dev' cannot be misread that way, matches what both docstrings promise, and is overwritten on the way to every real build.
deviations.authorized_by: Product Owner, asked before the edit with both options and their consequences; chose 'commit dev'. The task bullet's own stated intent ('harmless until someone reads it as the released commit') is what the literal instruction fails to deliver.
deviations.verified_how: Read the committed blob (`git show HEAD:src/environments/release.ts` before the change: f4ee01ce3c24b4326519ad99ae32ada05f7dd42b) and confirmed with `git cat-file -t` that it is a real commit object, not a sentinel. Confirmed the generator never writes 'dev' — scripts/generate-release.mjs:21-23 writes `git rev-parse HEAD` or falls back to 'unknown' — so the 'dev' placeholder only ever exists by being committed. Confirmed overwrite by running `pnpm build`, which rewrote the file to 8a5e12e, then restoring.

e2e.detail: pnpm test:e2e: 9 failed, 30 skipped, 386 passed (5.7m). Every one of the 9 is the same call — page.goto / first locator.click against the DS kit's own `python3 -m http.server` at e2e/helpers/ds-kit.ts:121-122, 'Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded' — which is the T389 harness flake T388 documented and owns. Proven a flake rather than a regression by re-running: --retries=2 gave 5 failed / 30 skipped / 390 passed, in a set DISJOINT from the first 9 (config, dashboard, home vs info, milestones, rsvp). The six affected spec files run serially with --workers=1 gave 4 failed / 131 passed, disjoint again; design-parity-info.spec.ts alone at --workers=1 gave 2 failed / 43 passed. No spec fails deterministically across four runs.
e2e.note: new_failures is empty and that is a claim, not an omission: the failing call never reaches app code — it is a navigation to a static file server serving ../wedding-ui-design's kit. This task changed a string constant read only by src/main.ts:49 (Sentry release) and removed an unused import from a guest-manager modal; neither is reachable from any of these specs. The flake is heavier on this machine than when T388 measured it (--retries=2 then left 0 failed / 3 flaky; here it leaves 5 failed), which is itself evidence for T389 and is filed under risks[].

risks.risk: The ds-kit e2e harness flake is materially worse than T388 measured. Four runs this session all failed on `openDsKitScreen` timeouts at e2e/helpers/ds-kit.ts:121-122, in a different set of specs each time, and --workers=1 did not fix it — so contention between the per-project `python3 -m http.server` instances is not the whole story, and T389's stated remedy (--retries=2, which left 0 failed for T388) no longer clears the suite here. Any task that reports a green e2e gate from now on is likely reporting a lucky run.
